newsitem.title: KENYA: Relief agencies say sanctions hurt Burundi.
newsitem.headline: Relief agencies say sanctions hurt Burundi.

text.p: Sanctions imposed on Burundi by regional leaders to punish a coup have severely cut humanitarian assistance and threaten the entire relief effort in the tiny Central African country, a U.N. official said on Monday.

"The regional embargo on Burundi declared on July 31 continues to impose severe restrictions on the ability of international humanitarian organisations to provide aid to the country's most vulnerable populations," Martin Griffiths said in a statement.

Griffiths, U.N. humanitarian coordinator for the Great Lakes region, said a regional sanctions committee last authorised international humanitarian organisations to import fuel on September 9, which was sufficient for only a month.
Griffiths said that since November 18, international organisations had made several unsuccessful joint requests for a new allocation of fuel since reserves were virtually depleted.
"Agencies are now being forced to consider reducing their emergency relief operations even further.

"If a favourable decision by the RSCC (sanctions committee) is not taken immediately, agencies will be unable to provide life-sustaining assistance to thousands of extremely vulnerable people in Burundi," Griffiths said.

It is not certain when the sanctions committee will meet but the presidents of Kenya and Uganda said in New Year statements that they still believed regional sanctions were the only way to persuade Burundi to restore full democracy.
The regional sanctions action followed a July 25 coup that brought retired army Major Pierre Buyoya to power.
